sections.body_md: You usually build trust through steady one-on-one conversations, reflection, and protected space. You tend to connect more deeply with people who enjoy discussing patterns, future possibilities, and meaning. In conflict you often default to harmony and emotional tone, so it helps to make your principles explicit. In close relationships and teamwork, you usually prefer flexibility, openness, and room to adapt.

sections.body_md: INFP-A and INFP-T share the same INFP core. Within values, empathy and personal meaning, the useful difference is how the two A/T styles handle confidence, pressure, feedback and self-correction, not which one is better.

content.quick_answer: INFP-A and INFP-T share the same INFP core. Within values, empathy and personal meaning, the useful difference is how the two A/T styles handle confidence, pressure, feedback and self-correction, not which one is better.

faq.answer: Around values, empathy and personal meaning, the main difference is usually confidence style, stress response, feedback processing and self-correction, not a change in the INFP core.
faq.question: What is the main INFP-A vs INFP-T difference?
faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.

faq.answer: No. A/T describes style differences, not a ranking. INFP situations can reward steadiness, caution or revision in different ways.
faq.question: Is INFP-A better than INFP-T?
faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.

faq.answer: Look at your response to values, empathy and personal meaning-related pressure, criticism, uncertainty and post-decision review rather than treating the label as a verdict.
faq.question: How can I tell whether I am INFP-A or INFP-T?
faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.

faq.answer: No. It can support INFP work-style reflection, but it should not replace skills, experience, values or context.
